transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Thank you for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this, I know you're very busy. 

Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just don't seem to have the push I used to have. For things I usually like, I mean. Like my choir, or my quilting, or even just visiting folks. I feel a bit awful saying it out loud, because I know people are expecting me to show up, but... most days I just sit at home. I just leave the TV on real low and sit there. I know I should be doing more, I really do, I just can't seem to get going. 

Does that make sense, Doctor? I hope I'm explaining it right for you.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Oh, well... it hasn't been all at once, Doctor. It's just sort of been... building up, I suppose. Nothing too dramatic, I promise. I'd say it really started after I retired from the school office. That was... oh, a little over two years ago now. 

I feel a bit terrible admitting it's been going on for that long. I kept thinking I'd just snap out of it and not have to bother anyone with it, you know? I really tried to just push through. Is it... is it okay that I waited to come in? I just hope I'm not making a mountain out of a molehill here.
During these past two years, have you had any stretches of time where you felt completely like your old self, or has this low mood been present most of the time?

Oh, gosh... I'm not entirely sure, Doctor. I... I haven't really kept track of it that closely, to be honest. I guess I just haven't noticed if there were stretches where I was completely my old self or not. 

I try not to dwell on things too much, you know, so I don't end up being a bother to anyone. I just sort of take each day as it comes. I hope that's an alright answer for you. I feel a bit silly not knowing for sure... I really don't mean to be unhelpful. Is it... is it bad that I can't give you a straight yes or no on that?
Looking back over these past two years, have there been any periods lasting two months or longer where you felt truly like yourself, with your normal energy and interest in your hobbies?

Oh, dear... two whole months? I... I don't think so, Doctor. I really wish I could say yes, just to give you some good news, but... no, I don't believe I've had a stretch that long where I felt completely right. 

I mean, I have good days! I don't want you to think I'm just miserable all the time, I really try to keep my chin up. Sometimes I'll get out to the store and have a nice chat with the cashier, and that feels good. But a whole two months of feeling like my old self with the choir and the quilting... no, I don't think I've managed that. 

I'm sorry, I feel like I'm failing a test or something, giving you all these gloomy answers. I hope I'm not being too difficult a patient for you today.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns or your appetite since you started feeling this way?

Oh, um... my sleep and appetite? I think they've been mostly fine, really. I mean, maybe a little different here and there, but nothing to worry about, I promise. 

I still eat my meals, you know, I try to make sure I'm taking care of myself so I don't worry my family. And as for sleep... well, I might toss and turn a bit some nights, but who doesn't at my age, right? I usually get enough rest to get by. 

I hope that's what you were asking? I just... I don't want to make it sound like I'm falling apart or anything. I'm doing my best to keep things normal. Is it okay that I haven't noticed any big changes there?
Do you often find yourself feeling inadequate or like you are not as capable as others?

Oh, my... well, I wouldn't say I feel inadequate, no. I mean, everyone has things they aren't the best at, don't they? I just try to focus on what I can do and leave the rest be. 

I certainly don't want to compare myself to others and get all down about it. I try to be helpful where I can, even if it's just little things around the house, so I'm pulling my weight. I hope that makes sense? I just... I really try not to let myself think that way, so I don't become a burden. I'm doing alright for someone my age, aren't I?
Do you often find yourself feeling hopeless about the future?

Oh, goodness, no... I really try not to let myself get like that. There's always something to be thankful for, isn't there? 

I mean, I know things aren't always perfect, but I try my hardest to look on the bright side. I certainly wouldn't want my family to think I've given up or anything like that. I just take it one day at a time and hope for the best. 

I think that's the right way to handle things, don't you? I just... I really don't want to sound like a complainer. I hope I'm answering these questions alright for you, Doctor.
Do you often find yourself being overly critical of yourself or feeling like you are not good enough?

Oh, um... overly critical? Well, I suppose everyone has moments where they wish they'd done something a little better, right? But I wouldn't say I'm too hard on myself. 

I really try to do my best with whatever I'm doing, whether it's keeping the place tidy or just... just managing my day. I don't sit around telling myself I'm not good enough, because I wouldn't want to bring anyone else down with that kind of talk. I try to keep my chin up. 

I mean, I'm doing okay, aren't I? I just try to be a good person and not cause any trouble for anyone. I hope that's the sort of answer you were looking for... I'm doing this right, aren't I?
When you are by yourself, do you ever find yourself feeling that you are not as good or as capable as the people around you?

Oh, um... no, not really. Even when it's just me in the house, I... well, I try to keep my mind occupied, you know? I don't sit there comparing myself to other folks. 

I think it's much better to just focus on what's right in front of you, like folding the laundry or fixing a little lunch. If you sit around feeling sorry for yourself or thinking you aren't good enough, well, that's just no good for anybody, is it? I always try to stay cheerful, even when it's quiet. 

I hope that's what you mean? I just... I try to be a good, capable person, doctor, and do my best with what I have. Am I making sense to you?
When you are feeling low, do you ever find yourself thinking that you are a failure compared to others?

Oh, my, no... I really wouldn't use a word like failure. I mean, we all have our little moments where we feel a bit blue, I suppose, but... no, I don't look at other folks and think I'm worse off or that I've failed. 

I've always just tried to do my best with what the good Lord gave me, you know? Just keep the house nice and mind my own business. I wouldn't want anyone thinking I'm ungrateful or sitting around feeling sorry for myself. That's just not the kind of person I am. 

I try to be strong and just keep going. Is that... is that the right way to look at it, doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the answers you need.
Do you ever find yourself feeling that you are not as worthy or valuable as other people?

Oh, goodness, no. I don't think like that. I mean, everyone has value, don't they? I've always believed that as long as you're kind to people and try to be helpful, well, you're doing just fine. 

I don't sit around thinking I'm less than anyone else. I just... I try to be a good neighbor and a good person. I wouldn't want to go around feeling sorry for myself or thinking I'm not worth anything. That just seems like a terrible way to live, and I wouldn't want to burden anyone with that kind of attitude. 

I just try to be positive and do what I can. I hope... I hope that shows that I'm doing alright? I'm answering these questions the right way, aren't I?
Do you often feel like you have less worth or value than other people?

Oh, heavens, I think we just talked about that, didn't we? But no, I really don't feel that way. I've always thought everybody has their own special place in the world, and I have mine. 

I don't go around measuring myself against the neighbors or anything. I just try to keep a clean home and be a nice lady. I wouldn't want you to think I have a bad attitude about myself. I'm perfectly content with who I am, really I am. 

Does that... does that sound like a healthy way to look at things? I just want to make sure I'm doing well in our little chat.
